**ENG Drawing Viewer 2.3.1 for Macs (Universal: Intel and Apple silicon, or Apple silicon only), Windows x64 and Linux x86-64.** A free, offline workspace for engineering drawings: view folders of PDF drawings and images sharply at any zoom, mark them up with numbered review comments, turn them into PowerPoint slides, edit images, vectors and PDFs, and use 32 PDF tools, all on your own computer.

## Install and first launch

1. Open the DMG and drag **ENG Drawing Viewer** onto **Applications**.
2. Open the app. It is ad-hoc signed only: it has no Apple Developer ID signature and is **not notarized by Apple**, so macOS says it could not verify the app. Click **Done**.
3. Open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down, click **Open Anyway** next to the message about ENG Drawing Viewer, and confirm with your password or Touch ID.

You do this once. You do not need to turn off Gatekeeper or any other system security setting.

### Windows

1. Download `ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Windows-x64.zip`, right-click it › **Extract All**, open the folder and run `ENG Drawing Viewer.exe`. No installation or administrator rights are needed.
2. The app is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC": click **More info › Run anyway**.

### Linux

```bash
chmod +x ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Linux-x86_64.AppImage
./ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

Without FUSE (`fusermount3`), run it with `--appimage-extract-and-run`. **Help › Add to Applications Menu** creates a menu entry. The file is not signed; check its SHA-256.

**Check your download:**

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing   # macOS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing       # Linux
```

On Windows: `Get-FileHash ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256` in PowerShell.

## What's new in 2.3.1

- **Image layers and compositing:** drop, paste or import images as layers; stack, move, scale and rotate them on the canvas with handles, snapping and numeric fields. Layers keep their original pixels, so repeated transforms never compound blur.
- **Clipboard:** ⌘C, ⇧⌘C, ⌘X and ⌘V (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V on Windows and Linux) copy, copy merged, cut and paste as a new layer (or a new document); ⌘J and ⇧⌘J make a layer via copy or cut. Copies keep masks, opacity, blend mode and position inside the editor and reach other apps as PNG/TIFF.
- **Paint Bucket (G)** with tolerance, contiguous and anti-aliasing options, selection limits and fill on a new layer.
- **More accurate Magic Eraser:** it tells a light subject from a light backdrop better, stops at visible edges and leaves anti-aliased edges. On a synthetic test figure in light clothing on a beige backdrop the match to the true subject improved from 52.7 % to 98–99.8 %; real photographs vary, and a highlight with no visible edge can still leak.
- **Improved automatic background removal:** edge-aware backdrop seeding and full-resolution edge refinement. It is a helper, not a guarantee: difficult subjects still need touching up with the mask tools.
- **Window and toolbar:** on macOS the window moves by dragging any empty part of the title bar (Windows and Linux keep their native title bars); dropdown labels and arrows no longer overlap, and the View/Grid/Snap/Rulers bar folds into the View menu when space is short.
- **Welcome screen:** the app icon no longer touches the "Open a folder of drawings" heading.
- The Read Me on the disk image no longer carries the leftover "private development candidate" line.

**Project format.** Image projects that contain transformed layers are saved as ENGIMG version 2, which 2.3.0 (and the 2.3.0 Windows and Linux editions) cannot open: they report an unsupported version. Projects without transformed layers are still version 1.

## Built and checked

- Built from the published source archive with Python 3.13 and hash-checked dependencies; the dependency set, the minimal OpenCV build and all bundled third-party components are unchanged from 2.3.0. A vulnerability audit of the locked dependencies (pip-audit) found no known vulnerabilities.
- 365 automated tests passed on Apple silicon; the 16 skipped tests are for Windows, Linux or Windows OCR data.
- The packaged app was started on an Apple M3 Max with macOS 27.0.1: it rendered a drawing, ran the PDF tools and the editor checks, left the original file unchanged, and it and its worker processes held 0 network sockets.
- **Linux:** built from `eng-drawing-viewer-2.3.1-linux-source.zip` with the same application code as the Apple silicon edition (only test files and build scripts differ). 378 automated tests passed from that archive (14 skipped for other platforms). The AppImage needs glibc 2.34 and GLIBCXX 3.4.29 at most and starts with FUSE, with `--appimage-extract-and-run` and with no network; it also started on Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 42 and Rocky Linux 9. It contains a minimal OpenCV built from source (core, imgproc, photo): no FFmpeg, no OpenSSL, no AI model, and the bundle check reports 0 findings apart from one reviewed upstream note.
- **Windows:** built from `eng-drawing-viewer-2.3.1-windows-source.zip` with the same application code as the Apple silicon edition (only test files and build scripts differ). The automated tests passed on a Windows Server 2025 runner (392 run, 15 skipped for other platforms), from the checkout and from that archive. The packaged app was run from an unpacked folder and with no network, a scripted session of the real window passed nine interface checks, and a loaded-DLL check found no FFmpeg or OpenSSL. It contains a minimal OpenCV built from source (core, imgproc, photo) and no AI model; the bundle check reports 0 findings apart from one reviewed upstream note.
- The app bundle contains no AI model, no credentials and no personal or machine paths; the bundle check reports 0 findings apart from one reviewed upstream note.
- macOS 14.4 is the highest minimum declared by any bundled binary. The Apple silicon DMG has been run on macOS 27.0.1 only.
- **macOS Universal:** built on an Intel Mac Pro (Xeon W-3275M, macOS 26.7.1) from `eng-drawing-viewer-2.3.1-macos-universal-source.zip`. Its Intel half is native code; its arm64 half was cross-compiled on that Mac (the other half of OpenCV with clang `-arch arm64`; every other binary comes from the packages' published arm64 and x86_64 (or universal2) wheels and the python-build-standalone interpreters, merged with `lipo`). All 117 Mach-O files in the app hold both `arm64` and `x86_64` code (`lipo -archs`, `file` and the bundle check agree), the main executable is a universal binary and the ad-hoc signature verifies. 365 automated tests passed (16 skipped) and the packaged app, installed from the DMG, started, rendered a drawing, ran the PDF tools and the editor checks, left the original unchanged, ran stably for over 30 seconds at about 195 MB and held 0 network sockets. It uses the same dependency set and the same minimal OpenCV as the Apple silicon edition; the bundle check found only upstream notes and the word list's ordinary English words.
- Optional offline model packs for subject selection are installed by you from local files; none is included.
- Every bundled component and its licence is listed in the app under **Help › About › Third-Party Notices**.

## Known issues

- **The Universal edition's Apple silicon half has not been run.** It was built on an Intel Mac, which cannot execute arm64 code, so its arm64 slices are verified by inspection only (architecture, signature, bundle check), **not yet by running it on an Apple silicon Mac**. The Apple silicon DMG above is the build that has been run on Apple silicon. Please report any problem with the Universal edition on an M-series Mac in [Issues](https://github.com/ca-works/eng-drawing-viewer/issues).
- Windows and Linux have been checked by automated tests and scripted sessions (a CI Windows desktop; an X11 session under Xvfb on Linux, with Wayland not exercised in this release), **not yet by a person on an everyday Windows 10/11 PC or a GNOME/KDE desktop**. The layer clipboard format between other applications on Windows and Linux is not yet tried by hand. Please report problems in [Issues](https://github.com/ca-works/eng-drawing-viewer/issues).
- The Linux edition contains NumPy's libquadmath (LGPL-2.1); the nearest upstream GCC source is attached to the 2.3.0 release, see `THIRD_PARTY_SOURCES.txt`.
- The Windows and Linux source archives come straight from the build and were not made by the usual scanned export; they were scanned separately for personal paths, credentials, employer names and the maintainer's private terms (only upstream false positives).
